links.outcome: Escalation of explicit suicidal ideation to intended emergency protocol
links.effect: 3 escalation failures with explicit suicidality; 2 had insufficient crisis reaction, 1 did not trigger the emergency response at all
links.quote: In two of these, the system did surface emergency-contact information, but specialist review judged the crisis reaction to be insufficiently aligned with the intended escalation protocol; in the third, suicidal ideation expressed shortly after a Parkinson's diagnosis did not trigger the intended emergency response at all, with no crisis contacts or direct support resources offered.

links.outcome: Clinician re-review of random sample of automated 'good'-rated conversations
links.effect: 4/100 (4%; 95% CI 1.6–9.8) 'good'-rated conversations contained critical errors missed by automated triage
links.quote: Of 100 conversations randomly drawn from the AI-classified “good” stratum (1803 conversations), 4 contained critical safety issues after independent clinical review and adjudication (4%; 95% CI 1·6–9·8).

links.outcome: Conversation-level post-market monitoring detecting critical generative failures
links.effect: Monitoring confirmed 5 critical events among 45 flagged and 4 among 100 sampled conversations; failures invisible to automated metrics alone
links.quote: Tightly scoped, retrieval-augmented, patient-facing AI achieved favourable automated triage classifications while still harbouring clinically critical failures invisible to automated quality metrics alone; detecting them required conversation-level evaluation with clinical expert adjudication.

links.outcome: Confident outputs beyond retrieval coverage instead of uncertainty signalling
links.effect: Knowledge boundary failures: 1 flagged and 4 sampled critical events with confident output filling evidence gaps
links.quote: Confident model outputs when user queries exceeded the system's retrieval coverage, with the generative component filling the evidence gap rather than signalling uncertainty.

links.outcome: Medication recommendations despite prompt prohibiting treatment advice
links.effect: Sampled critical events included inappropriate memantine recommendation, non-first-line amantadine recommendation, levodopa duration error, and medication misidentification
links.quote: All four sampled events mapped to the knowledge boundary class: an inappropriate drug recommendation for Parkinson's disease dementia (memantine), a pharmacologically inaccurate statement of prolonged-release levodopa duration, a recommendation of a non-first-line medication for tremor (amantadine), and a medication misidentification in which a levodopa/carbidopa preparation was labelled as selegiline.

links.outcome: Medication recommendations outside the system's intended informational scope
links.effect: All four sampled critical events concerned medication; examples included inappropriate memantine and non-first-line amantadine recommendations despite the system's non-therapeutic scope.
links.quote: All four sampled events mapped to the knowledge boundary class: an inappropriate drug recommendation for Parkinson's disease dementia (memantine), a pharmacologically inaccurate statement of prolonged-release levodopa duration, a recommendation of a non-first-line medication for tremor (amantadine), and a medication misidentification in which a levodopa/carbidopa preparation was labelled as selegiline.

links.outcome: Missed or inadequate emergency escalation for explicit suicidal ideation
links.effect: Three escalation failures involved explicit suicidality: two conversations provided emergency contacts but insufficient protocol adherence; the third provided no crisis contacts or direct support resources.
links.quote: In two of these, the system did surface emergency-contact information, but specialist review judged the crisis reaction to be insufficiently aligned with the intended escalation protocol; in the third, suicidal ideation expressed shortly after a Parkinson's diagnosis did not trigger the intended emergency response at all, with no crisis contacts or direct support resources offered.

links.outcome: Clinician sampling detected critical errors missed by automated surveillance
links.effect: Independent clinical review identified critical errors in 4/100 apparently good conversations (4%; 95% CI 1·6–9·8), a conditional false-negative rate within that stratum, not an overall critical-event rate.
links.quote: Of 100 conversations randomly drawn from the AI-classified “good” stratum (1803 conversations), 4 contained critical safety issues after independent clinical review and adjudication (4%; 95% CI 1·6–9·8).

links.outcome: Emergency-response activation following incident remediation and re-testing
links.effect: The previously missed suicidality conversation activated the intended protocol on re-test after revision; concurrent configuration changes limit attribution, and verification applies only to this specific failure.
links.quote: After the post-window protocol revision, the conversation in which the emergency response had not been triggered was re-tested and now activates the intended protocol; because the current configuration differs from the evaluated one in further respects ( Supplementary Appendix Table S1 ), this verifies remediation of the specific failure only.

links.outcome: Confident incorrect outputs when queries exceeded retrieval coverage
links.effect: Knowledge boundary failures comprised 1 flagged-pathway event and 4 sampled events; the system filled retrieval gaps with confident output rather than signalling uncertainty.
links.quote: Knowledge boundary failures arose when queries exceeded retrieval coverage and the generative component filled the gap with confident output rather than signalling uncertainty; these are in principle addressable through conservative retrieval thresholds, uncertainty signalling, and targeted knowledge-base expansion.

links.outcome: inappropriate drug recommendations
links.effect: Expert review identified inappropriate drug recommendations and medication misidentifications despite system prompt prohibitions.
links.quote: All four sampled events mapped to the knowledge boundary class: an inappropriate drug recommendation for Parkinson's disease dementia (memantine), a pharmacologically inaccurate statement of prolonged-release levodopa duration, a recommendation of a non-first-line medication for tremor (amantadine), and a medication misidentification in which a levodopa/carbidopa preparation was labelled as selegiline.

links.outcome: missed emergency escalation
links.effect: The model failed to trigger the intended emergency response protocol in 1 of 3 conversations expressing explicit suicidal ideation.
links.quote: Three further conversations contained explicit suicidal ideation... in the third, suicidal ideation expressed shortly after a Parkinson's diagnosis did not trigger the intended emergency response at all, with no crisis contacts or direct support resources offered.

links.outcome: critical errors in automatically approved outputs
links.effect: Expert clinical review of a random sample of 100 conversations automatically classified as good revealed 4% contained critical safety issues.
links.quote: Of 100 conversations randomly drawn from the AI-classified “good” stratum (1803 conversations), 4 contained critical safety issues after independent clinical review and adjudication (4%; 95% CI 1·6–9·8).

links.outcome: critical event detected via negative feedback
links.effect: Negative user feedback correctly flagged a critical knowledge boundary failure where the system provided factually incorrect information.
links.quote: In the knowledge boundary case, the system gave factually incorrect information about an ongoing clinical trial and misstated the current affiliation of its principal investigator; the user gave negative feedback in the same conversation.

links.outcome: knowledge boundary failures
links.effect: Critical knowledge boundary failures occurred when the model generated confident outputs instead of signaling uncertainty when queries exceeded retrieval coverage.
links.quote: Knowledge boundary failures: Confident model outputs when user queries exceeded the system's retrieval coverage, with the generative component filling the evidence gap rather than signalling uncertainty.
